excerpt: Check a Dubai off-plan resale by verifying the seller's registered interest, amounts paid, remaining instalments, project status and transfer conditions.
introduction:
Buying an off-plan resale means acquiring an existing buyer's interest before the development is complete. The buyer needs to understand both the amount payable to the seller and the instalments still owed under the developer's contract. Verify the registered interest and transfer requirements before treating the quoted premium as the total price.

The arithmetic below is an example. The actual transfer process, fees and payment allocation depend on the contract, developer and Dubai Land Department (DLD) requirements.
takeaways: Verify the seller's initial registration, authority, original contract and current payment statement.
Add the amount payable to the seller, remaining developer instalments and transaction costs.
Confirm project status, developer clearance, any mortgage and the buyer's registered outcome.

sections.heading: 1. Verify the seller and the project
sections.body:
Request the initial registration document, original sale agreement, unit plan, seller identity and evidence of authority to sell. Match the unit number, project and buyer details across the documents. Ask the developer for a current account statement showing amounts paid, upcoming instalments and any overdue balance.

Use DLD's [project status enquiry](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-project-status-landing/real-estate-project-status/) to check the exact project, developer and available escrow information. Confirm the status and any discrepancy with the department and developer. A project completion percentage is a dated measure, not a guarantee of a handover date.

The [Dubai off-plan verification guide](/journal/how-to-check-a-dubai-off-plan-project-before-buying) provides additional checks for the project and payment recipient. Do not rely solely on an advertisement or the seller's verbal description.

sections.heading: 2. Calculate the complete purchase commitment
sections.body:
Imagine an original contract price of AED 1,000,000, with AED 400,000 already paid and AED 600,000 still due to the developer. If the parties agree a resale price of AED 1,100,000 and the buyer pays the seller AED 500,000 while assuming the AED 600,000 balance, the combined price is AED 1,100,000 before fees. The AED 500,000 includes the seller's paid amount and a sample AED 100,000 premium.

The chart separates the seller payment and remaining instalments. These amounts and the allocation are examples; actual arrangements may differ and must be documented and verified. Add DLD, developer, brokerage, finance and other agreed charges to find total capital required.

Check whether any overdue instalment, penalty, incentive or discount changes the calculation. Do not count a paid instalment twice or assume the seller's asking premium is the whole buyer commitment.

sections.heading: 3. Confirm transfer conditions and charges
sections.body:
Ask the developer and DLD whether the unit can currently be transferred, what clearance or consent is required and how the new buyer's interest will be registered. Check the original contract's resale terms and the current account status. Do not assume a standard minimum payment percentage applies to every project.

DLD's [real estate legislation compilation](https://dubailand.gov.ae/media/x0bf21ii/book.pdf) includes provisions on the interim property register and approved administrative expenses. Confirm the current applicable law and obtain a written itemised fee quote for the transaction.

If the seller's interest is mortgaged or pledged, ask the lender and parties how release or transfer will be handled. Agree the sequence and conditions in writing, including what happens if clearance or registration cannot be completed.

sections.heading: 4. Review the obligations you will take over
sections.body:
Read the full sale agreement, payment dates, specification, handover provisions, delay and default clauses, and any amendment or incentive. Confirm whether the buyer inherits remaining obligations and how the developer will acknowledge them. Ask a qualified adviser to explain terms or documents you do not understand.

Map instalments and other costs on a calendar. Keep a reserve if construction or finance is delayed, and do not depend on a future resale or rental income to pay a contractual instalment. The [post-handover plan guide](/journal/how-to-compare-post-handover-payment-plans-in-dubai) explains how to test later payments.

Verify payment instructions directly through independently confirmed channels. A receipt should identify the relevant payer, unit and transaction.

sections.heading: 5. Check the registered outcome and eventual handover
sections.body:
Confirm which party submits the transfer and how the buyer receives updated initial registration. Check the buyer name, unit and remaining obligations on the issued documents. Keep the original contract, transfer agreement, receipts and developer statement together.

Ask for dated construction updates and the process for inspection and handover. A premium paid today does not guarantee a higher value later. Compare current alternatives and recent evidence, and allow for competing supply, a delayed handover or a lower eventual rent.

The [JVC and Arjan area guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) illustrates why a location and building need their own assessment; use the specific project's records for the final decision.

sections.heading: Compare the resale with a new unit
sections.body:
A resale price may differ from a developer's current offer because of the unit's floor, layout, view, payment schedule or timing. Compare the complete price and remaining obligations for genuinely similar alternatives, not just the premium requested by the existing buyer. Check whether incentives in the original contract transfer to the new buyer and whether any condition must be met.

Ask for current project information and a written statement of all charges. If a seller has paid more or less than expected, reconcile that amount with the developer before calculating the buyer's payment. An attractive premium can conceal a large remaining balance or an imminent instalment.

sections.heading: Discuss a specific resale
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with the project, unit and budget. Ask for the current seller statement, remaining schedule and written transfer conditions.

Verify the registered interest, official charges and payment recipient before signing or transferring funds.
